description: Block 2: New York session-window module (America/New_York, DST-aware) with the 8:30 and 9:30 manipulation legs, plus IST display. Fully objective (no unconfirmed subjective rule), so it is built first. Independent of the other detector blocks except that later blocks import its session/leg classification.
steps: Create v1_lab/ny_session.py, pure Python stdlib only (matching v1_lab/qm_detect.py style: module docstring stating scope + LOCKED vs tunable, argparse CLI, load_ohlc reuse, print_summary, --selfcheck).

Reuse the OHLC loader from qm_detect.py (import load_ohlc from qm_detect, or a shared _io) so bar datetimes are parsed identically. Bar timestamps in the CSVs are naive; treat them as the data's native exchange/server clock. Document the assumption explicitly and expose a --data-tz parameter (default: the timezone the CSV is already in) so the mapping to New York is not silently hard-coded. Do NOT guess the broker offset - make it a parameter with a documented default and note it must be confirmed against the actual MT5 export.

Implement provable DST math as an explicit function ny_utc_offset(date) returning -4 (EDT) for dates from the 2nd Sunday of March through the day before the 1st Sunday of November, else -5 (EST). Compute the 2nd-Sunday-of-March and 1st-Sunday-of-November boundaries arithmetically (do not hard-code specific years).

Cross-check ny_utc_offset against Python's zoneinfo ZoneInfo('America/New_York') inside selfcheck() for a range of sample dates spanning both DST transitions and multiple years, asserting they agree. zoneinfo is available in this sandbox (verified).

Implement session classification for New York: a function that, given a bar's New-York local time, returns whether it falls in the NY session and flags the 8:30 and 9:30 legs. Treat 8:30 and 9:30 as two SEPARATE, EQUALLY-labelled manipulation legs (leg tags like 'ny_0830' and 'ny_0930'); do NOT hard-code one as 'manipulation' and the other as 'expansion'. Expose the NY session window bounds and the leg definition windows as parameters with documented defaults.

Provide an IST display helper (convert a New-York local or UTC time to Asia/Kolkata for user-facing output) and use it in print_summary so counts are shown with IST timestamps alongside NY, per the display-in-IST requirement.

Add a --selfcheck with synthetic timestamps proving: (a) DST offset matches zoneinfo across transition dates and years; (b) a known UTC/NY instant maps to the correct IST wall-clock (e.g. NY 08:30 EDT -> the correct IST time), and that the mapping shifts correctly after a DST change; (c) the 8:30 and 9:30 legs are tagged distinctly and neither is labelled manipulation-vs-expansion; (d) a bar just outside the NY window is classified as not-in-session (boundary test).

Add a real-data run path: `python3 v1_lab/ny_session.py v1_lab/XAUUSD_M15_clean.csv` that tags every bar and prints counts of total bars, in-NY-session bars, 8:30-leg bars, 9:30-leg bars, with the date range shown in both NY and IST. Optionally write a per-bar session-tag CSV via --out.
acceptance_criteria: `python3 v1_lab/ny_session.py --selfcheck` prints 'selfcheck: PASS' and all four assertion groups (DST-vs-zoneinfo, IST mapping incl. post-DST shift, distinct 8:30/9:30 legs, session boundary) pass.
ny_utc_offset returns -4/-5 with boundaries computed arithmetically and agrees with zoneinfo for every sampled date across at least two years including both transitions.

Running on v1_lab/XAUUSD_M15_clean.csv prints deterministic counts (total bars, in-NY-session, 8:30-leg, 9:30-leg) and shows the date range in both NY and IST; running twice yields byte-identical --out CSV.

No 8:30/9:30 leg is hard-coded as manipulation vs expansion; both are neutral, equally-labelled legs. No unconfirmed subjective rule is baked in; the data->NY tz mapping and window bounds are parameters.
verification: python3 v1_lab/ny_session.py v1_lab/XAUUSD_M15_clean.csv --out v1_lab/ny_tags.csv  (record printed counts)
Run the previous command twice and confirm md5sum of v1_lab/ny_tags.csv is identical (determinism)
findings: Implemented v1_lab/ny_session.py (pure stdlib: csv, datetime, argparse, zoneinfo). Reuses load_ohlc from qm_detect via sys.path insert so timestamps parse identically and it runs from repo root. DST implemented as explicit arithmetic ny_utc_offset(date): 2nd Sunday of March (via _nth_weekday_of_month) through the day before 1st Sunday of November = EDT -4, else EST -5; no years hard-coded. Self-check: 'selfcheck: PASS' with all four groups - (a) ny_utc_offset agrees with ZoneInfo('America/New_York') at noon over 2023-2026 incl. both transition Sundays +/-1 day; (b) NY 08:30 -> IST 18:00 EDT / 19:00 EST (shifts exactly 1h across DST); (c) legs tagged distinctly ny_0830 / ny_0930, both neutral (no manipulation-vs-expansion labels); (d) session boundary 09:29 out / 09:30 in / 16:00 out (exclusive end). data->NY mapping is a --data-tz parameter (documented default America/New_York, flagged as MUST-confirm against the real MT5 export - many brokers use EET/EEST). Session window (default 09:30-16:00) and both leg windows (08:30-09:30, 09:30-10:30) are parameters. Real-data run on v1_lab/XAUUSD_M15_clean.csv (22849 bars): total=22849, in-NY-session=6581, ny_0830-leg=1016, ny_0930-leg=1015; date range NY 2025-08-01 01:00 -0400 .. 2026-07-27 10:00 -0400, IST 2025-08-01 10:30 +0530 .. 2026-07-27 19:30 +0530. Determinism: md5sum of v1_lab/ny_tags.csv identical across two runs (37d6254a9408d03eca4a875c4c30c8a5). py_compile passes. Public importable functions for later blocks: ny_utc_offset, to_ny, to_ist, classify_ny, tag_bars, load_ohlc (re-exported).
